name: Origin Dollar Vault mintMultiple reentrancy
summary: VaultCore.mintMultiple() skipped the supported-asset check that mint() performed, so the attacker passed a self-controlled fake stablecoin whose transferFrom re-entered the vault and triggered a rebase between the first mint's asset transfer and its OUSD supply increase, minting more OUSD than the vault held in assets.

loss.notes: Origin's project post-mortem reports a $7 million loss. PeckShield independently estimated approximately $7.7 million, including 11,809 ETH and 2,249,821 DAI, so the record retains Origin's rounded first-party gross-loss figure without presenting the reported token quantities as exact structured components.

ageReset.description: The last of 11 pre-incident Upgraded events selected the defect-bearing Vault implementation from topic 1.

sources.note: Reviewed the successful Ethereum receipt and full call trace, the VaultProxy and implementation creation transactions, every pre-incident Upgraded event, historical runtimes, Origin's project post-mortem, and PeckShield's technical analysis. Attack contract 0x47c3d84394043a4f42f6422accd27bb7240fdfe2 calls mint(address,uint256), mintMultiple(address[],uint256[]), and redeem(uint256) on VaultProxy 0x277e80f3e14e7fb3fc40a9d6184088e0241034bd; each call delegates to 0x328d15f6b5eba1c30cde1a5f1f5a9e35b07f5424. This execution reproduces the missing supported-asset validation and reentrant fake-token path described by the post-mortems. The proxy was directly deployed by 0xaed9fdc9681d61edb5f8b8e421f5cee8d7f4b04f at block 10884566:67. Its 3,422-byte runtime is unchanged through the exploit. A complete scan finds 11 Upgraded events from deployment through the pre-exploit block; the final event is log 206 at block 11247976:82 and selects implementation 0x328d15f6b5eba1c30cde1a5f1f5a9e35b07f5424 from topic 1. That implementation was directly deployed at block 11246268:118, and its 13,075-byte runtime hashes to 0xbe4bcad9eaca1eff00cd54018ab0ba94901a5f078b0b24dfe560d9a7f012371d at deployment, activation, and immediately before the exploit. Origin reports a $7 million loss; PeckShield estimates approximately $7.7 million.

limitations: The $7 million gross loss is Origin's rounded project-reported USD figure; PeckShield's independent estimate is approximately $7.7 million.
